Increasing pain, swelling, and stiffness in left knee nine months after total knee arthroplasty

Which was replaced with a prosthetic joint 9 months ago. She reports that the knee had been healing well after surgery until about 3 weeks ago, when she began noticing increasing stiffness and mild warmth.
outpatient visit, Cardiology, Dr. Michael Rodriguez
Six-month history of worsening fatigue, lightheadedness on standing, and two episodes of near-syncope

This 75-year-old female with diabetes, hypertension, vascular dementia, right hemiparesis, and recent left knee prosthetic infection presents to the clinic with a 6-month history of increasing fatigue and episodes of lightheadedness, particularly when she stands up from a sitting position. She also reports two instances of near-syncope over the past month.
outpatient visit, Endocrinology, Dr. Aisha Patel
Episodes of morning confusion, abnormal behavior, and diaphoresis before breakfast

The patient presents to Endocrinology in the context of Type 2 diabetes mellitus, vascular dementia, and prior cerebrovascular accident, following recent Cardiology evaluation for sinus bradycardia and prior prosthetic joint infection. She admits to occasional mild tremors and sweating during these episodes but does not recall confusion.
inpatient visit, Internal Medicine, Dr. James O'Brien

Following prior endocrinologic and orthopedic complications, she has been bedridden for the past week due to weakness and has a Foley catheter in place.
ed visit, Emergency Medicine, Dr. James O'Brien
Caregiver reports decreased activity, poor oral intake, and chronic sacral wound with increased drainage
The patient with prior Stage I sacral ulcer presents with increased drainage. She is wheelchair-bound and incontinent of urine for two days.
ed visit, Emergency Medicine, Dr. Maria Gonzalez
Generalized weakness, right arm pain, and unexplained bruising in the setting of advanced dementia

The patient is a 78-year-old female with vascular dementia, residual right-sided hemiparesis, and a history of recurrent pressure ulcers including Stage III sacral involvement documented in prior encounters. She returns to the emergency department accompanied by her son with complaints of generalized weakness and pain in her right arm.

lines: Dorothy is a 75-year-old woman here for wound and heart rhythm follow-up. Her son Robert coordinates appointments; a home aide is present during the day.
Dorothy may be confused, especially in the morning. Speak clearly and involve Robert and the aide in instructions.
She values her care team working together. Check with Dorothy before answering, if possible.
Avoid using terms related to dementia, stroke, or abuse in front of her or in written materials.
She is wheelchair-bound and needs help with daily activities.
